items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: No it’s something — the Gettysburg Address for me has always been a very important thing... Lincoln threw down — basically he said look this is what this nation is really all about... ever since I first heard the Gettysburg Address in elementary school it always stuck with me.

ctx.x: It’s really interesting to revisit that speech now. Did you come across it again and then make a connection or is it something you thought of?

No it’s something — the Gettysburg Address for me has always been a very important thing, not because it signaled the end of slavery, it didn’t, also it signaled the end of separatism, meaning the south asserting its contention that as a Confederate group of — not states, I don’t want to call them states — provinces or as a group of individual former states that we have the right to separate ourself out even though we said initially that we were going to part of this United States. Just because we don’t like the…

that we bear as Americans anyway, trying to figure out our sins that we need to really atone for. Because we haven’t atoned — I mean slavery is one of them, various other things that we’ve done to people, I’m talking about within our country under the guise of either states’ rights or the majority rules or whatever. I mean there are several levels of redress that we still need to address as a nation. So to me that has always been the epitome of one of the challenges that still remains in front of us. Lincoln…
